questions.question: Which among the following comes under tertiary sector of Indian Economy?
questions.solution: The tertiary sector includes service industry and it holds the highest importance among all sector. The Tertiary sector of economy involves the provision of services to business as well as final consumers. Services may involve the transport, distribution and sale of goods from producer to consumers.

questions.question: _______ publishes Economic Survey in India.
questions.solution: Finance Ministry of India presents the Economic Survey in the parliament every year, just before the Budget. It is prepared under the guidance of the Chief Economic Adviser, Finance Ministry.

questions.question: In which economic system the government decides what goods are to be produced in accordance with the needs of society?
questions.solution: In a socialist society, the government decides what goods are to be produced in accordance with the needs of society. It is assumed that the government knows what is good for the people of the country and so the desires of individual consumers are not given much importance.

questions.question: 1 Rupee note bears the signature of whom?
questions.solution:
Under Section 22 of the Reserve Bank of India Act, RBI has sole right to issue currency notes of various denominations except one rupee notes.

The One Rupee note is issued by Ministry of Finance and it bears the signatures of Finance Secretary, while other notes bear the signature of RBI Governor.

questions.question: Which five year plan recognized human development as the core of all developmental efforts?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is the **Eighth Five Year plan.**

 
• The Eighth five-year plan was launched after the inflation during 1990-91. It ran for a period of 5 years from 1992-1997.
 
• The main objective was to create employment, curb population growth, and to achieve overall human development.
 
• The major highlight of this plan was the modernisation of industries.
 
• The country achieved a growth of 6.8% against the target growth of 5.6%.

questions.question: A system of rules that takes effect when a military authority takes control of the normal administration of justice is called as _______.

questions.solution:

questions.question: For a time difference of two hours, the longitudinal distance will be equal to ________.
questions.solution:
Every one-degree shift of longitude corresponds to 4 minute time difference.

So a time difference of 1 hour (60 minutes) will have:

1 degree = 4 minutes

So, 60/4 = 15 and 15 × 1° = 15°

Now for 2 hours (120 min)

1 degree = 4 minutes

120/4 = 30 and 30 × 1° = 30°

So a time lag of 2 hours corresponds to 30 degrees of longitudinal change.

This follows from a simple fact that 360∘ ⇒ 24 hours.

Which is same as 360° ⇒ 1440 min. So 1° ⇒ 1440/360 = 4 minutes.

questions.question: Who built Red Fort (Agra) in Delhi?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Akbar**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Agra Fort**, also known as the **Red Fort of Agra**, due to the extensive use of red sandstone in its construction.
 
• It was** built predominantly by Emperor Akbar in 1565 AD**, with subsequent additions by Shah Jahan and Aurangzeb, the Agra Fort is not just a fort but more of a walled city.
 
• It covers an area of approximately 94 acres, complete with palaces, mosques, and gardens.
 
• The fort combines different architectural styles, with a blend of Hindu and Islamic elements.
 
• Its notable structures include the Jahangir Palace, Diwan-i-Am, Diwan-i-Khas, and the Moti Masjid. 
 
• Of particular historical interest is the fact that Shah Jahan, who added ornate white marble structures to the fort was imprisoned here by his son, Aurangzeb.
 
• He spent his final seven years in a tower with a view of the Taj Mahal, which he built in memory of his wife, Mumtaz Mahal.
 
• Today, Agra Fort is a UNESCO World Heritage site, open for tourists who want to experience India's rich history.

questions.question: Which among the following do not participate in election of the President?

options.text: Elected members of both the houses
Elected members of legislative assemblies of states
Elected members of legislative assemblies of Delhi and Puducherry

questions.solution:
• Nominated Members of the Parliament do not take part in the election of the President of India.
 
• President is elected by an electoral college consisting of elected members of parliament and Elected members of all State legislative assembly and Delhi and Pondicherry.
 
• He must have completed the age of 35 years to contest for Presidential elections. He must be a citizen of India.
 
• Article 54 and 55 provides for the election of the President.

questions.question: Which among the following metals was not found in Harappan civilization?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Iron** was not used in the Harappan cities.
 
• Harappan cities are part of Indus Valley Civilizations, which was held after the **Chalcolithic period of stone-age**.
 
• During the Chalcolithic period,** copper** was first used to make tools, utensils, and other objects.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Indus civilization, also known as the Indus Valley Civilization or the** Harappan Civilization**, is the oldest known urban culture of the Indian subcontinent.
 
• The atomic dates of civilization appear to be around** 2500 to 1700 BCE**, although the southern sites later moved into the second millennium BCE. 
 
• The civilization was first identified in** 1921** in Harappa in the Punjab region and then in **1922 in Mohenjo-Daro** (Mohenjodaro) near the Indus River in the Indus (Sindh) region.
 
• Both sites are in the provinces of **Pakistan, Punjab, and Sindh** respectively.
 
• The ruins of Mohenjo-Daro were designated as a **UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1980.**

questions.question: In which continent 'Great Dividing Range' is located?
questions.solution: The Great Dividing Range is located in Australia. It is so called because it forms a watershed. Rivers on the east side flow from the highlands toward the Pacific Ocean; on the west side they flow toward the central lowlands. questions.question: Which of the following cells organ are present only in plant cell?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Plastids**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The plastids are the cell organelles found in all the **plant cells**.
 
• They bear some specific pigments, thus imparting specific colors to the plants.
 
• Three types of plastids are:
 
 
• Chloroplast - contains Chlorophyll(Green pigment)
 
• **Chromoplast** - contains Carotenoid(Red, Yellow, and orange pigment)
 
• **Leucoplast** - contains colorless plastid, mainly stores foodstuff in a plant cell.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
 

 
 
__Cell Part__

 
 
 
__Function__

 
 
 

 
 
Lysosomes

 
 
 
 
• Lysosomes are small sac-like structures surrounded by a single membrane and containing strong digestive enzymes.
 
• The lysosome is also known as a suicide bag of the cell.
 
 
 
 

 
 
Mitochondria

 
 
 
 
• The mitochondria are round "tube-like" organelles that are surrounded by a double membrane, with the inner membrane being highly folded.
 
• The mitochondria are often referred to as the "powerhouse" of the cell.

questions.question: Muscles are connected to bones by connective tissue called as _____.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Tendon**__.

Tendons:

__
 
• Tendons are fibrous connective tissue.
 
• Tendon connects muscle to bone.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• Cartilages__:

 
 
• It is a type of connective tissue in the body.
 
• It is a strong, flexible tissue that is the main type of connective tissue in the body.
 
• Due to the presence of Cartilages in our ears, the ears can be folded.
 
• Elastic cartilage is a type of cartilage present in the outer ear.
 
• It doesn’t have blood vessels or nerves.
 
• This tissue is present in joints, ears, nose, rib cage, and in many other areas of the body.
 
 
 
• Bones:
 
 
• Bones in our bodies are living tissues that make up the skeleton.
 
• It provides shape and support to the body, as well as protection for some organs in the body.
 
• The Femur is the strongest bones of the human body.
 
 
 
• Ligaments:
 
 
• It is a short, fibrous, and elastic connective tissue.
 
• It attaches bone to bone, gives support to the joints. 
 
 
 
• Adipose is a connective tissue that stores energy in the form of fat.

 i.e., The angle of incidence (θ i ) = Angle of reflection (θ r )

questions.question: Protocol used for receiving an email is _____.
questions.solution: Post Office Protocol version 3 (POP - 3) is a standard mail protocol used to receive emails from a remote server to a local email client. POP - 3 allows you to download email messages on your local computer and read them even when you are offline.

questions.question: Tartaric Acid is **not** found in _____.
questions.solution: Tartaric acid is a white crystalline diprotic organic acid. The compound occurs naturally in many plants, particularly in grapes, bananas, and tamarinds. It is also one of the main acids found in wine. Oxalic acid is a natural product found in spinach.

questions.question: What is the chemical name of quick lime?

questions.question: In a periodic table, while moving from left to right in a period, number of _____ remains same.
questions.solution: In a periodic table atomic size gradually decreases from left to right across a period of elements. This is because, within a period or family of elements, all electrons are added to the same shell.
